title: Néron lft-models under ramification-one base change and strict-local descent
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring, $K=\operatorname{Frac}R$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$, and let $V/K$ be a smooth separated commutative finite-type group scheme [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. A commutative group scheme has multiplication, identity and inverse morphisms satisfying the commutative group diagrams. Separated means that its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Locally of finite type and finite type have the meanings of [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. A Néron lft-model of a smooth separated finite-type group $V$ over the fraction field $F$ of a DVR $D$ means a smooth separated $D$-group $M$, with specified generic-fibre identification $M_F=V$, for which restriction $\operatorname{Hom}_D(X,M)\to\operatorname{Hom}_F(X_F,V)$ is bijective for every smooth $D$-scheme $X$ [def-pc-base-change, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. (i) If $M/S$ is a Néron lft-model of $V$ and $R\to A$ is a local injective extension of DVRs for which a uniformizer of $R$ generates the maximal ideal of $A$ and the residue-field extension is separable, then $M_A$ is a Néron lft-model of $V_{\operatorname{Frac}A}$. This includes $A=R^{\mathrm{sh}}$, a strict henselization [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization]. The open subgroups of fibrewise identity components commute with these base changes; an identity component means the connected component containing the identity in a geometric fibre [def-weil-connected-scheme]. (ii) Conversely, if $D=R^{\mathrm{sh}}$, $F=\operatorname{Frac}D$, and $M'/D$ is a Néron lft-model of $V_F$ with the specified generic identification, there is a smooth separated commutative Néron lft-model $M/S$ of $V$ and a group isomorphism $M_D\simeq M'$ inducing that generic identification. The model and the isomorphism are unique up to unique group isomorphism inducing the identity on $V$. Neither $M$ nor $M'$ is required to be quasi-compact.

source.place: BLR 10.1 Proposition 3, printed p.290 (PDF p.296), and strict-henselian descent in Proposition 7 proof, printed p.293 (PDF p.299); compare 6.5 Theorem 1 and Corollary 3, printed pp.157–159, whose finite-type descent argument is applied to finite unions of components containing the generic fibre Primary scan read at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf. Local PDF WANTED; agent-extracted formulation of the indicated argument.

proof.text: First, smoothness and separatedness of $M_A$ follow by base change: apply the smooth base-change clause locally at the relative dimension of each point and pull back the closed diagonal. The group operations are the base changes of those of $M$; their identities are equalities of the corresponding composites, so are preserved. The generic fibre is $V_{\operatorname{Frac}A}$ by associativity of fibre products. Let $A\hookrightarrow B$ be an injective local extension of DVRs with $B\cong\mathcal O_{X,x}$ for a point $x$ of a smooth $A$-scheme $X$; locality puts $x$ over the closed point. [lem-sfb-essentially-smooth-dvr-index-one] gives $\mathfrak m_AB=\mathfrak m_B$ and a separably generated residue extension $\kappa(B)/\kappa(A)$, which is separable by [lem-weil-pbc-separably-generated-separable]. Then $\mathfrak m_RB=(\mathfrak m_RA)B=\mathfrak m_AB=\mathfrak m_B$, and [lem-sfb-separable-field-extension-transitivity] applied to $\kappa(R)\subseteq\kappa(A)\subseteq\kappa(B)$ makes $\kappa(B)/\kappa(R)$ separable. Thus $R\hookrightarrow B$ satisfies exactly the hypotheses of the valued-point approximation lemma; no separability of the fraction-field extension is inferred.

source.place: BLR 10.1 Proposition 3 and 7.2 Theorem 1 second proof, pp.290,177

proof.text: Given $v\in V(\operatorname{Frac}B)$, apply [lem-sfb-index-one-valued-point-smooth-approximation] to $R\hookrightarrow B$, $W=V$ and $v$. Obtain $a:\operatorname{Spec}B\to U$ with $U/R$ smooth and $h:U_K\to V$ restricting to $v$. The mapping property of $M$ extends $h$ to $\widetilde h:U\to M$. The composite $\widetilde h a$ is a $B$-point of $M_A$ over $A$ with generic point $v$. Hence every essentially smooth DVR test for $M_A$ is surjective. Apply [lem-sfb-neron-dvr-point-criterion] over $A$ to conclude that $M_A$ is a Néron lft-model. The construction uses only finite-type $V$ and one smooth affine approximation at a time, and never quasi-compactness of $M$.

source.place: BLR 10.1 Proposition 3 via Proposition 2, printed p.290; 3.6 Proposition 4, printed p.79

proof.text: For $D=R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ relative to the chosen separable closure $k^s$ of $\kappa(R)$, fix an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $k^s$ and the geometric point $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ at the closed point. [lem-exc-affine-strict-local-ring-comparison], applied to $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$ with the identity affine open, gives an $R$-algebra isomorphism $\theta:\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{\operatorname{Spec}R,\bar s}\simeq D$ and identifies the residue field of $D$ with $k^s$; in particular $\kappa(D)/\kappa(R)$ is separable algebraic, hence separable in the possibly transcendental sense. Through $\theta$, [lem-sc-strict-henselization-dvr] makes $D$ a DVR with injective local structural map. The maximal-ideal equality is [lem-sc-ring-strict-henselization-local-maximal-ideal]. Step 2 therefore applies to $A=D$. For any of the base changes in (i), [lem-sbc-section-component-cartesian] applied to the structure map and the identity section identifies its fibrewise identity-component locus with the inverse image of the original one.

source.place: BLR 2.3 Proposition 10, printed p.50; 10.1 Proposition 3; Stacks more-morphisms.tex Tag 055M, lemma-base-change-connected-along-section

proof.text: The component loci just used are open even when the group is not quasi-compact. Around a point of the locus, choose a quasi-compact open $W$ of the smooth separated group containing that point and the entire identity section (the base trait is quasi-compact). Its structure map is quasi-compact and quasi-separated over the Noetherian trait. The identity section factors through $W$. Apply [lem-sbc-smooth-section-component-open]: its section-component locus is open in $W$, contains the chosen point if $W$ contains its whole fibre component, and is contained in the group component locus. Such a $W$ exists: on a geometric fibre [lem-sfb-locally-algebraic-group-identity-component] makes the identity component quasi-compact, and [lem-sbc-section-component-cartesian] says its image covers the original component (every original fibre point lifts: the tensor product of its residue field with an algebraic closure of the base field is a nonzero ring and has a prime); add finitely many affine neighbourhoods covering it. This proves openness. On geometric fibres the identity components are subgroups by the same group lemma; the operations therefore factor through these open loci. Step 3 identifies the loci under base change, and identical open subsets with their restricted structure sheaves give the same open subgroup schemes.

source.place: Stacks more-morphisms.tex Tags 055R and 055M; groupoids.tex Tag 0B7R; BLR 10.1 following Definition 1, p.290

proof.text: For (ii), fix a uniformizer $\pi\in R$. Put $T_n=\operatorname{Spec}(D^{\otimes_R n})$ and $U_n=T_n[1/\pi]$. Since $D$ is a DVR with maximal ideal generated by $\pi$, $D[1/\pi]=F$. The mapping property of $M^{\prime}/D$ is thus the generic-extension property in [lem-sfb-generic-extension-ind-etale-limits]. Its tensor-power clause gives that property for every pullback of $M^{\prime}$ to $T_2$ or $T_3$. This applies over the entire tensor-product ring, which need not be a DVR; it would be invalid to apply the DVR base-change clause directly to that ring. The generic identification with $V_F$ gives a canonical group isomorphism $\alpha_\eta:p_0^*M^{\prime}|_{U_2}\simeq p_1^*M^{\prime}|_{U_2}$.

source.place: BLR 6.5 Corollary 3 proof, printed p.159, ind-étale limit expansion

proof.text: Use the extension property of the target $p_1^*M^{\prime}$ with the smooth test scheme $p_0^*M^{\prime}$ to extend $\alpha_\eta$ to $\alpha$ on $T_2$. Extend its inverse in the other direction. Their composites restrict to the identity; injectivity of restriction makes them identity globally. On $T_3$, both $p_{12}^*\alpha\circ p_{01}^*\alpha$ and $p_{02}^*\alpha$ restrict to the same canonical generic isomorphism, so they agree. Similarly compare the two maps from $(p_0^*M^{\prime})^2$ expressing multiplication compatibility, the maps from $T_2$ expressing identity compatibility, and the maps from $p_0^*M^{\prime}$ expressing inverse compatibility. Each source is smooth and each pair agrees on $U_2$, so injectivity gives all three identities. Thus $\alpha$ is a group-compatible descent datum, including its cocycle.

source.place: BLR 6.5 Corollary 3 proof, printed p.159: construction, cocycle and group compatibility

proof.text: First, $M^{\prime}$ is commutative: the multiplication of $M^{\prime}$ and its composite with the swap of factors are two maps from the smooth $D$-scheme $M^{\prime}\times_DM^{\prime}$ which agree on the generic fibre because $V_F$ is commutative, so they are equal by injectivity in the mapping property of $M^{\prime}$. Thus $M^{\prime}$ is a smooth separated commutative Néron lft-model over the DVR $D$, and by [lem-sfb-neron-lft-finite-set-affine] every finite subset of $M^{\prime}$ has an affine open neighbourhood. Its generic fibre is $V_F$, of finite type by assumption and base change. Step 6 supplies the group-compatible datum with the prescribed generic datum. These are all the hypotheses of [lem-sfb-strict-henselian-lft-group-datum-effectivity]; apply it to obtain a smooth separated commutative $R$-group $M$ and $M_D\simeq M^{\prime}$ with $M_K\simeq V$. This step uses effectivity for locally finite-type groups, not finite-type effectivity applied to the whole $M^{\prime}$.

source.place: BLR 6.5 Theorem 1 with 10.1 Proposition 7 descent, printed pp.157–159,293

proof.text: Let $X/R$ be smooth and $f_K:X_K\to V$. Its pullback to $F$ extends uniquely to $f_D:X_D\to M^{\prime}\simeq M_D$. On the double overlap, the two pullbacks of $f_D$, compared by $\alpha$, agree after inverting $\pi$. They are equal by injectivity of the extension property from Step 5, with smooth source $X_{T_2}$. The faithfully flat map $R\to D$ of [lem-sc-strict-henselization-faithfully-flat] is an affine fpqc cover; its base change $X_D\to X$ is an fpqc cover by [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] to the compatible maps $X_D\to M$ to obtain a unique map $X\to M$. Its generic restriction equals $f_K$ because equality can be tested after the same fpqc base change of $X_K$. If two extensions existed, their pullbacks to $D$ would agree by the mapping property of $M^{\prime}$, and fpqc uniqueness would make them equal. Hence $M$ has the full Néron mapping property for every smooth $X$, without quasi-compactness.

source.place: BLR 6.5 Corollary 3 proof, p.159; Stacks descent.tex Tag 023Q, lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms; more-algebra.tex Tag 07QM

proof.text: If $M_1,M_2$ are two models with their generic identifications, their mapping properties extend $1_V$ uniquely to maps $M_1\to M_2$ and $M_2\to M_1$. The composites are identities by uniqueness. The map commutes with multiplication by applying the same uniqueness to the smooth source $M_1\times_R M_1$, and similarly to identity and inverse. Its pullback to $D$ agrees with the prescribed comparison to $M^{\prime}$ because both induce the same generic map and $M^{\prime}$ has the mapping property. This proves the asserted uniqueness of the model together with its comparison.

The BLR PDF is not under literature/, so I checked the BLR-derived statements mathematically and on small cases. Stacks 030U/030W were read for the added node; no SGA is cited. Four faults, repaired in fixes/. (1) C5/D1: the first clause of new node lem-sfb-essentially-smooth-dvr-index-one-tower duplicates the existing base node lem-sfb-essentially-smooth-dvr-index-one (Q36, same unit). Step 1 now cites that node, plus lem-weil-pbc-separably-generated-separable and a new unsplit statement-only node lem-sfb-separable-field-extension-transitivity (reviewer-added, created.item = this item). m_R B = m_B is now derived inline, and the tower node is dropped. (2) C4: step 3 applied lem-sc-strict-henselization-dvr and the triples lemma, both stated for other constructions, to the def-sc strict henselization. Step 3 now uses lem-exc-affine-strict-local-ring-comparison: θ: O^sh ≅ D, residue field k^s, and DVR status transported through θ. The triples lemma is removed. (3) E1: step 7 used commutativity of M′, which both cited nodes require, without deriving it. It now proves it: m and m∘swap agree generically, so they are equal by Néron injectivity. (4) B2: the corollary sentence of lem-sfb-generic-extension-ind-etale-limits used R without introducing it; R is now introduced as a local ring, with no change of content. Other checks: steps 2 and 4–6, 8 and 9 are correct (DVR point criterion hypotheses, 055R on a qc open W containing the whole fibre identity component, cocycle and group compatibility on T_2/T_3, fpqc descent via 07QM, 022D and 023Q). The approximation, ind-étale and effectivity statements were tested (R→R̂ with an inseparable fraction field extension, t a unit or nilpotent, Galois orbits of components) and found plausible; none is a duplicate and none restates the item. The statement and base change are unchanged. Batch 5: the closure of lem-sfb-neron-dvr-point-criterion reaches lem-trf-smooth-reduced-dense-pullback, lem-trf-normal-topologically-noetherian-components and lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change. These are generic scheme theory, not steps of the trace formula or Poincaré duality proofs, so I accept them. The added cites add nothing to that closure and create no cycle.
